title: Peregrine Retail partner outreach scratchpad
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Prospect: Peregrine Retail (mid-market omnichannel retailer, ~1.2k employees). Focus: home goods, DTC + wholesale. HQ in Minneapolis.
- Why target: heavy personalization roadmap (site search, product recs, support triage), high volume of short-text inference (search queries, chat, personalization rules). Likely needs: predictable latency, cost control, private deployment for PII/POI in loyalty data, and can benefit from Dedicated capacity for peak sales events.
- Goal for sequence: secure intro call with VP of Engineering (Nora Patel) and Head of Personalization (Jamal Ortiz). Objective: qualify infra/security needs, propose pilot (3-week POC) using Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on infra constraints.

Notes from quick research (signals to use in outreach):
- Tech stack hints: Shopify Plus storefront + custom headless React front-end. Backend on AWS (EC2/EKS). Uses Segment for events.
- Data residency: serves US and EU customers, mentions GDPR in job postings — potential need for EU-hosted deployment or VPC controls.
- Recent job posts: Sr. ML Engineer, ML infra (Jan 2025) — suggests ramping ML initiatives.
- Past PR: awarded "fast-growing" retailer article Nov 2024 — execs are growth-minded.
- Likely pain: token costs at scale, model latency spikes during flash sales, limited observability into per-route inference costs.

Stakeholders to map (notes + intro hooks):
- Nora Patel — VP Eng (decision maker for infra and security). Hook: predictable SLAs for peak shopping events, VP cares about uptime and integrations with existing infra.
- Jamal Ortiz — Head of Personalization (ML owner). Hook: improved throughput for real-time personalization, cheaper at-scale inference, eval/regression alerts to avoid degrading UX.
- Priya Singh — Head of Customer Support (ops). Hook: deflection via chat + faster response times; limited engineering resources to maintain self-hosted models.
- Procurement — expects committed capacity pricing; may prefer annual reserved capacity.

Outbound cadences (A/B test drafts)
A) Short cold email (value-first)
Subject: Reduce inference cost + latency for Peregrine personalization
Hi Nora —
Saw Peregrine’s recent push on personalization and your job opening for ML infra — congrats on the growth. We work with retailers (Shopify Plus/Headless) to run LLM-powered personalization at predictable cost and latency by combining Dedicated pools and smart batching/caching.
Quick ask: 15-min intro next week to share a couple recommendations (one is a non-invasive 3-week pilot) and a case study from a similar retailer that cut per-session inference costs ~45%?
— Maya Chen, Redwood Inference

B) Slightly longer, technical trigger callout
Subject: Short pilot idea for Peregrine — private inference + per-route observability
Hi Jamal —
Noticed your personalization team is hiring ML infra talent. We’ve been helping teams move from ad-hoc endpoints to a unified inference runtime that gives token-level cost breakdowns, automatic KV/prefix caching, and rollback-safe rollouts. Typical pilot includes: one model served in our Dedicated pool (or VPC private deployment), simple A/B routing, and an eval deck for quality monitoring.
Interested in a 20-min sync? I can bring Diego (solutions eng) to answer infra questions.

C) LinkedIn DM (concise)
Hi Nora — Maya at Redwood. Quick question: do you have a current SLA for personalization inference latency during peak? We help retailers get predictable tail-latency with minimal infra changes. 2 quick slides?

Call agenda (30 mins) for discovery meeting if intro accepted:
- 5m quick intros + context about Peregrine’s personalization goals
- 10m current architecture + traffic shapes (p99 latency targets, QPS at peaks, typical sequence length)
- 5m security/compliance constraints (EU residency, KMS, audit logs)
- 5m example pilot plan + success metrics (cost per session, p99 latency, quality regressions)
- 5m next steps and ownership (solutions eng + procurement touchpoints)

Key qualification questions (to ask early):
- Can you share rough QPS during normal and peak windows for personalization endpoints? (helps sizing Dedicated pool)
- Where is customer data stored today? Any hard EU residency requirements?
- Do you prefer SAAS-hosted API or self-hosted/private deployment?
- Are there internal cost targets per session / per-user personalization?
- How do you currently detect quality regressions when models change? Manual tests or evals?

Objection handling (short bullets):
- "We already have a self-hosted model infra": acknowledge investment, propose hybrid (start with Redwood Dedicated for overflow/peak and integrate slowly), show how KV caching and batching can reduce cost without touching their model training.
- "Security / data residency concerns": highlight Private deployment (VPC + on-prem option), KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. Offer an architecture diagram and SAML/SCIM for SSO.
- "Cost is unclear / vendor lock-in concerns": provide transparent per-token math, show rollback and export capabilities, and offer a short-term POC with cost tracking. Emphasize routing policies that can fallback to cheaper model variants.
- "We don’t have time to run a pilot": offer a ‘read-only’ demo and a sandbox with synthetic traffic mirroring their distribution so engineering time is minimal.

Pilot (3-week) proposal (starter template)
Week 0: kickoff + infra checklist (networking, basic keys, test data schema)
Week 1: deploy one model to Dedicated pool + smoke test using synthetic/real traffic for 24h
Week 2: enable prefix/KV caching, set up batch configs, run load tests to simulate peak
Week 3: A/B routing + quality monitoring + cost report and handover doc; final review with metrics and recommended production rollout plan
Success criteria (pick any 2-3):
- p99 latency under X ms (TBD during discovery)
- >=30% reduction in per-session inference cost vs current baseline
- No regression in top-100 QA prompt set (linked)

Pricing anchors / negotiation notes:
- For mid-market retailer: propose a pilot credit + discounted first 3 months on Dedicated capacity if they commit to 6-12 month reserved capacity.
- Procurement will push for capped overage and clear exit terms (data export). Have template contract clause from legal for private deployments.

Internal asks (who to loop in)
- Solutions Eng: Diego Ramos — availability to join first meeting and answer infra/network questions.
- Product: Evelyn Brooks — to outline observability/rollout features and any eval templates.
- Legal/Security: need quick ATO checklist for VPC/private and EU-data flow notes.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Get a copy of the top-100 personalization prompts from Jamal during discovery to add to our eval deck.
- Prepare a short synthetic traffic generator mirroring Peregrine’s session length distribution (ask SRE for sample scripts).
- Pull the "retail personalization case study" numbers (where we saved the deck?) — check Confluence ID CONFLUENCE-RET-203.
- Draft minimal SOW template for 3-week pilot for procurement review.

Quick scripts to use on call (verbatim lines):
- "If we could reliably drop your per-session inference cost by 30% while keeping p99 latency the same, is a short pilot worth exploring?"
- "We’ve seen teams adopt Dedicated capacity for predictable peaks and then move to hybrid Private later — would that be a path that makes sense for you?"

Notes-to-self: stay lightweight on pricing until we understand QPS and sequence distribution. Prioritize getting the model/traffic signals; everything else flows from that.

Last updated: 2025-03-03 by Maya Chen.
